title: MGE Energy, Inc. Prices Public Offering of 3,300,331 Shares of Common Stock
summary: Madison, Wis., May 6, 2026—MGE Energy, Inc. (Nasdaq: MGEE) (MGE Energy) announced today that it has priced its previously announced underwritten public offering of 3,300,331 shares of its common stock at a public offering price of $75.75 per share. Of the 3,300,331 shares of common stock being offered, MGE Energy agreed to issue and sell directly 990,099 shares to the underwriters in the offering, and the forward sellers (as defined below) agreed to borrow from third parties and sell to such underwriters 2,310,232 shares of common stock in connection with the forward sale agreements described below. In conjunction with the offering, MGE Energy has granted to the underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to 495,049 additional shares of its common stock. If such option is exercised, MGE Energy may, in its sole discretion, enter into additional forward sale agreements with the forward purchasers with respect to such additional shares or issue and sell such shares directly to the underwriters.
body_text: Madison, Wis., May 6, 2026—MGE Energy, Inc. (Nasdaq: MGEE) (MGE Energy) announced today that it has priced its previously announced underwritten public offering of 3,300,331 shares of its common stock at a public offering price of $75.75 per share. Of the 3,300,331 shares of common stock being offered, MGE Energy agreed to issue and sell directly 990,099 shares to the underwriters in the offering, and the forward sellers (as defined below) agreed to borrow from third parties and sell to such underwriters 2,310,232 shares of common stock in connection with the forward sale agreements described below. In conjunction with the offering, MGE Energy has granted to the underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to 495,049 additional shares of its common stock. If such option is exercised, MGE Energy may, in its sole discretion, enter into additional forward sale agreements with the forward purchasers with respect to such additional shares or issue and sell such shares directly to the underwriters. Morgan Stanley, Guggenheim Securities, BofA Securities and J.P. Morgan are acting as joint book-running managers for the offering. Closing of the offering is expected to occur on or about May 8, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. In connection with the offering, MGE Energy entered into separate forward sale agreements with each of Morgan Stanley, BofA Securities and J.P. Morgan or their respective affiliates, referred to in such capacity as the forward purchasers, pursuant to which MGE Energy agreed to sell to the forward purchasers the same number of shares of common stock as are borrowed from third parties and sold by the forward purchasers or their affiliates (in such capacities, the “forward sellers”) to the underwriters. Under the forward sale agreements, the forward purchasers agreed, upon physical settlement, to purchase shares from MGE Energy at an initial forward sale price per share equal to $72.9094, subject to certain adjustments that are made to that price over the term of each forward sale agreement. Settlement of the forward sale agreements is expected to occur no later than approximately 20 months after the date of the prospectus supplement for the offering. MGE Energy may, subject to certain conditions, elect cash settlement or net share settlement for all or a portion of its rights or obligations under the forward sale agreements. MGE Energy intends to use the net proceeds from the sale of shares of common stock in the offering for general corporate purposes, which may include repayment of short-term debt; repurchases, retirements and refinancing of other securities; funding capital expenditures; and investments in subsidiaries. MGE Energy will not initially receive any proceeds from the sale of the common stock sold by the forward sellers to the underwriters. MGE Energy intends to use any net proceeds that it receives upon settlement of the forward sale agreements as described above. A shelf registration statement on Form S-3, including a prospectus, related to the shares, has been filed by MGE Energy with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC") and has become effective automatically upon filing. The offering will be made only by means of a preliminary prospectus supplement and the accompanying prospectus which has been filed with the SEC. Copies of the preliminary prospectus supplement and the accompanying prospectus, and the final prospectus supplement, when available, may be obtained from Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, Attn: Prospectus Department, 180 Varick Street, 2nd Floor, New York, New York 10014; Guggenheim Securities, LLC, Attention: Equity Syndicate, 330 Madison Avenue, New York, New York 10017 (email: gsequityprospectusdelivery@guggenheimpartners.com ); BofA Securities, Inc., Attn: Prospectus Department, NC1-022-02-25, 201 North Tryon Street, Charlotte, North Carolina 28255-0001 (email: dg.prospectus_requests@bofa.com ); or J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, c/o Broadridge Financial Solutions, 1155 Long Island Avenue, Edgewood, New York 11717 or by email at prospectus-eq_fi@jpmchase.com or by visiting the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov . This press release shall not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy these securities, nor shall there be any sale of these securities in any state or jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities laws of any such state or jurisdiction. About MGE Energy MGE Energy is a public utility holding company. Its principal subsidiary, Madison Gas and Electric (MGE), generates and distributes electricity to 170,000 customers in Dane County, Wis., and purchases and distributes natural gas to 180,000 customers in seven south-central and western Wisconsin counties. MGE's roots in the Madison area date back more than 150 years. title: Avery Dennison® Expands Supreme Wrapping Film™ Portfolio with Five New Trend-Setting Colors
summary: Avery Dennison® (NYSE:AVY) Graphics Solutions debuted five new colors for its flagship Supreme Wrapping Film™ color change vehicle wrapping film product line. These strategic color additions provide installers with high-demand finishes that bridge the gap between luxury aesthetics and the reliable, professional-grade performance the industry expects from the SW900 series.
body_text: Avery Dennison® Expands Supreme Wrapping Film™ Portfolio with Five New Trend-Setting Colors MENTOR, Ohio – May 28, 2026 – Today Avery Dennison® (NYSE:AVY) Graphics Solutions debuted five new colors for its flagship Supreme Wrapping Film™ color change vehicle wrapping film product line. These strategic color additions provide installers with high-demand finishes that bridge the gap between luxury aesthetics and the reliable, professional-grade performance the industry expects from the SW900 series. Avery Dennison debuted five new colors of its Supreme Wrapping Film™ color change vehicle wrapping film product line. Pictured from left to right, the colors are Gloss Ivory, Gloss Metallic Gothic Rose, Gloss Sand Dune, Matte Metallic Oasis Blue, and Satin Metallic Cyber Green. All five films deliver the easy conformability Supreme Wrapping Film is known for by shops and installers worldwide. The new additions to the Avery Dennison portfolio include: Gloss Ivory - A sophisticated light beige that redefines "Quiet Luxury" Gloss Sand Dune - A timeless, medium beige designed to mirror modern OEM paint finishes Satin Metallic Cyber Green - An electric finish that captures light across every curve with a smooth, metallic glow Matte Metallic Oasis Blue - A serene turquoise blue that evokes ultimate tranquility Gloss Metallic Gothic Rose - A deep, moody rose with a heavy metallic flake for a premium custom-paint appearance Gloss Ivory Supreme Wrapping Film from Avery Dennison is a sophisticated light beige that redefines ‘Quiet Luxury. SW900 Gloss Sand Dune offers a timeless, medium beige designed to mirror modern OEM paint finishes. An electric finish that captures light across every curve with a smooth, metallic glow – this is the new SW900 film color Satin Metallic Cyber Green from Avery Dennison. The Spring 2026 Supreme Wrapping Film collection includes Matte Metallic Oasis Blue, which is a serene turquoise blue that evokes ultimate tranquility. The new Avery Dennison Supreme Wrapping Film color Gloss Metallic Gothic Rose is a deep, moody rose with a heavy metallic flake for a premium custom-paint appearance. "The stunning new tones in the Avery Dennison spring collection have been carefully curated to reflect the latest shifts in automotive styling," said Brittany Folino, Senior Product Manager for Avery Dennison Graphics Solutions. "These finishes allow the professional restyling community to offer their clients unique, trend-forward looks while maintaining the highest standard of installation quality." Avery Dennison Supreme Wrapping Film combines an extensive color change collection with more than 140 film colors. The films deliver outstanding durability, 3D conformability and performance, custom versatility and installation convenience. Supreme Wrapping Film color change vehicle wraps feature Avery Dennison Easy Apply™ RS technology. This innovation makes application faster and easier, regardless of the applicator's skill level. The technology enables installers to reposition the film and easily press out any wrinkles and bubbles. Moreover, the film and technology combination ensures excellent conformability around challenging curves and recesses. "This latest extension signifies our commitment to the rising demand for premium finishes that perform as well as they look," Folino said. "Supreme Wrapping Film continues to be the professional's first choice because it delivers the quality and client satisfaction required in high-end restyling." For more information about Supreme Wrapping Film colors, visit graphics.averydennison.com/swf . Join the conversation on Avery Dennison Graphics Solutions' social channels, including Facebook and Instagram . About Avery Dennison #MakingPossible Avery Dennison Corporation (NYSE: AVY) is a global materials science and digital identification solutions company. We are Making Possible™ products and solutions that help advance the industries we serve, providing branding and information solutions that optimize labor and supply chain efficiency, reduce waste and mitigate loss, advance sustainability, circularity and transparency and better connect brands and consumers. We design and develop labeling and functional materials, radio-frequency identification (RFID) inlays and tags, software applications that connect the physical and digital and offerings that enhance branded packaging and carry or display information that improves the customer experience. Serving industries worldwide — including home and personal care, apparel, general retail, e-commerce, logistics, food and grocery, pharmaceuticals and automotive — we employ approximately 35,000 employees in more than 50 countries. Our reported sales in 2025 were $8.9 billion. Learn more at www.averydennison.com . Images © 2026 Avery Dennison Corporation. All rights reserved. Used with permission.

title: How to Keep a Character Consistent in Nano Banana
summary: Nano Banana, Google's Gemini image model, is praised for character consistency: supply reference images of your subject and edit conversationally to place the same face in new scenes. Nano Banana Pro blends up to fourteen references and holds up to five subjects.
body_text: HOW IT WORKS STEP 1 PROVIDE REFERENCE IMAGES Give Nano Banana one or more clear images of your subject, a person, pet, mascot, or product, to define the identity. Made in Flick STEP 2 PROMPT THE NEW SCENE Ask in natural language to place that same subject in a new scene or pose, telling it to keep the face and outfit. Made in Flick STEP 3 BLEND REFERENCES WITH FUSION Combine multiple references, such as the character plus a wardrobe or background, into one image while preserving identity. Made in Flick STEP 4 REFINE WITH CONVERSATIONAL EDITS Iterate with edits like changing the lighting while keeping the face. Identity holds across edits, though it can soften after many changes. Made in Flick STEP 5 BRING IT TO LIFE IN FLICK Nano Banana makes stills only. Drop your consistent character into Flick and animate it with Veo 3, Kling, or Seedance. Made in Flick

title: Time and Half Pay: Calculations, Rules, and Compliance
summary: Learn how time and half pay works, including calculations, overtime rules, and compliance tips to ensure your business stays on track.
body_text: You probably know the moment already. A project runs long, a few people stay late to finish client work, and payroll gets a stack of timesheets that don't quite agree with what managers remember seeing. In a mid-sized agency, that's where time and half turns from a math term into a real payroll risk, because one missed adjustment can flow into every pay run after that. The federal rule is simple on paper. Under the Fair Labor Standards Act , most nonexempt employees must be paid at least 1.5 times their regular rate for hours worked beyond 40 in a workweek , and the law has used that overtime premium since 1938 ( Congressional Research Service overview of FLSA overtime ). In practice, the hard part is not the formula, it's the data. If payroll input is late, incomplete, or split across tools, the premium gets misapplied and the cost shows up later in corrections, back pay, and audit cleanup. For teams trying to integrate payroll with fund accounting , that kind of mismatch is exactly where the work gets messy. Why time and half trips up even experienced payroll teams A lot of agency leaders assume overtime mistakes come from bad math. In practice, the failures usually start earlier, with late approvals, inconsistent time entries, and too many hands on the same hours before payroll closes. I've seen the same pattern repeat in mid-sized marketing firms and professional services shops. A strategist logs client calls at the end of the week, a project manager edits a timesheet after approval, and finance discovers too late that the week crossed the 40-hour line. Under federal law, the overtime trigger sits inside a fixed, recurring 168-hour workweek, not the calendar week your team sees on a planner, so weekend or holiday work only matters if it pushes total hours over the threshold in that defined week ( U.S. Department of Labor overtime guidance ). What time and half means Time and half is the federal overtime premium, not a bonus. It means a nonexempt employee gets paid at least 1.5 times their regular rate for each hour beyond 40 in the workweek, and the employee may still work any number of hours if the schedule needs it, because the rule controls pay, not scheduling ( CRS FLSA report , DOL overtime guidance ). A weekly premium can look small in isolation and still distort an agency's numbers fast. A mid-sized marketing firm with client service, creative, and account teams may have one account running hot while another stays under budget, so a single misclassified overtime rate can throw off project margins, utilization reports, and client billing in the same pay period. That difference matters because overtime is a recurring cost line that shows up in payroll runs again and again. If your team handles multiple clients or cost centers, one wrong premium rate can contaminate reporting long after the check clears, and the correction often lands in a later period where managers no longer remember who approved the extra hours. Practical rule: treat overtime as a compliance issue first and a payroll calculation second. If the hours are wrong, the rate won't save you. When agencies run clean payroll, they pair time tracking with accounting controls early. That matters when you try to integrate payroll with fund accounting , because the same discipline that keeps payroll clean also keeps job costing, approvals, and labor allocation from drifting apart. A team that closes time late can still pay people, but it pays for the mistake later in corrections, audit questions, and manual cleanup. How to calculate time and half across common payroll scenarios A payroll run can look correct at first glance and still miss the overtime premium. That happens in agencies and professional services firms when the regular rate shifts because of bonuses, commissions, salaried nonexempt status, or fluctuating workweek arrangements, while the spreadsheet keeps treating every extra hour the same. Workforce.com explanation of time and half , Paychex guidance on calculating time and half, Tennessee MTAS fluctuating workweek reference The standard formula is still simple. Multiply the employee's regular hourly rate by 1.5 , then multiply that overtime rate by the number of overtime hours. If someone earns $20 per hour , the overtime rate is $30 per hour because $20 × 1.5 = $30 . Start with the basic hourly example For a worker at $20 per hour who logs 45 hours , the first 40 hours are paid at the regular rate and the extra 5 hours are paid at $30 per hour . That part is easy, which is exactly why payroll teams sometimes stop checking once the first row balances. The test is whether your process handles the cases that do not fit the clean hourly example. In agency payroll, that is where errors usually start, because one missed rule can carry through client billing, project margin reporting, and payroll corrections in the same cycle. Watch the regular rate when pay is variable Bonuses, commissions, and incentives can change the regular rate, which means they can change the overtime amount too. If a nonexempt employee receives extra pay tied to work in the same week, payroll cannot assume the original hourly rate still applies. Salaried nonexempt employees create another common trap. If the salary covers only straight-time pay for the first 40 hours , overtime still applies when the employee works beyond that point, and the regular rate has to be recalculated from that week's actual hours and eligible pay components. Mid-sized firms get caught here when they rely on a fixed template instead of checking what went into that week's pay. Use the fluctuating workweek rule only when the facts fit The fluctuating workweek method works differently. Because the fixed salary is treated as covering straight-time pay for all hours worked, the overtime premium is only half-time , not full time and a half, and the calculation adds 0.5× the regular rate for each hour over 40 . That can lower overtime cost per extra hour, but only if the salary is fixed and the arrangement meets FLSA requirements. In real payroll reviews, teams often assume the method applies because the employee is salaried, then discover the setup never met the rule in the first place. Pay structure Regular rate Overtime rate Example (45 hours) Hourly, standard overtime Hourly wage 1.5× regular rate 5 hours at overtime rate, plus 40 regular hours Salaried nonexempt, straight overtime Weekly salary converted to regular rate 1.5× regular rate Recalculate from that week's hours, then pay the premium Fluctuating workweek Weekly salary divided by hours worked 0.5× regular rate 5 hours at half-time premium, if the method applies Variable pay with bonus or commission Base rate plus eligible extras in the regular rate 1.5× adjusted regular rate Recompute the overtime rate before payroll closes If the regular rate changes, the overtime rate changes with it. That is the part that breaks manual reviews. For teams that still build overtime in spreadsheets, a clean starting point is the timesheet Excel formula guide , but spreadsheets only help if the input is already right. Federal and state overtime rules that affect your agency Federal law gives you the floor, not the whole rulebook. The FLSA's 40-hour overtime trigger is the baseline, but state law can set stricter rules, and in those states you can't stop at the federal minimum ( U.S. Department of Labor overtime guidance ). The salary threshold also keeps moving, which affects who counts as exempt. Historical markers in the record show the threshold at $455 per week in 2004 and about $23,660 annually , then $684 per week in 2019 and about $35,568 annually , then $844 per week effective July 1, 2024 , and $1,128 per week effective January 1, 2025 ( NBER overtime study and history of threshold changes ). That means a job title alone never settles the question, and an old exemption memo can age out. Why the workweek definition matters The FLSA defines a workweek as a fixed, regularly recurring 168-hour period, or seven consecutive 24-hour days ( DOL overtime guidance ). That definition matters because payroll sometimes treats Sunday through Saturday as the only valid window, then misses overtime that belongs to a different internal pay cycle. The legal clock is the defined workweek, not the calendar your team uses for project planning. For agencies with employees across states, this gets even more delicate. Some states use daily overtime thresholds or double-time rules, so a federal-only review can leave a gap even when the U.S. baseline looks clean. A useful state-specific reference for one example is Arizona overtime law guidance , but the larger point is simple, every state file needs its own check. What changed in the salary thresholds The repeated threshold changes tell you something about compliance work. It is not static, and old payroll rules do not stay safe just because they once passed review. When a threshold changes, exemption status can change too, which means a manager who looked exempt last year may need overtime protection this year. Managers often remember the title, but payroll has to track the threshold. That gap is where agencies get surprised. They keep the same job structure, the same approval chain, and the same assumptions, then one updated salary rule turns a long-standing arrangement into a liability. Compliance mistakes that cost agencies thousands The most expensive overtime errors usually look boring in the moment. A manager classifies someone as exempt because the role sounds senior. Payroll runs the check without reworking the regular rate. Finance assumes weekend work automatically earns premium pay. Each of those shortcuts can leave a gap. Historical research found that noncompliance with time and half rules has been material for decades, with the share of covered workers who worked overtime but did not receive the legally required premium reported in the range of 25% , and one dataset showing almost 16% of covered overtime workers did not receive time and half ( NBER study ). That is why this issue keeps showing up in audits. It's not rare, it's easy to miss. The mistakes I see most often Misclassifying exempt employees: A job title sounds exempt, but the salary threshold or duties test may not support it. Skipping regular-rate updates: Bonuses and commissions change the overtime base, so the rate from last week may no longer be right. Treating weekends as automatic overtime: Weekend work only triggers premium pay if total hours cross the 40-hour line in the FLSA workweek. Confusing calendar weeks with the legal workweek: Payroll can use a calendar view for planning, but compliance still follows the fixed 168-hour period. Trusting old settings in payroll software: If the system is still built around last year's threshold or method, it will keep making the same mistake. That list sounds basic until you review a file set with mixed pay types, multiple states, and last-minute approvals. Then it starts looking like a pattern, because the errors usually come from the same place, weak input control. Where agencies stay exposed Professional services firms are especially vulnerable when managers spread hours across client work, internal meetings, and business development. A timesheet that looks fine at the task level can still hide an overtime problem at the week level, because payroll cares about total compensable hours, not just the work category. I've also seen teams assume salaried workers are safe from overtime review. They're not, if they're nonexempt and the salary only covers straight time, the overtime premium still applies, and the calculation has to be right before the pay run closes. How calendar-based tracking eliminates overtime errors and timesheet fatigue Manual timesheets create the same problems over and over. People log time late, round differently, or forget low-friction work like internal meetings and quick client calls. By the time payroll sees the file, the week is already closed, and the cleanest fix is usually a correction instead of prevention. Calendar-based tracking gives operations a different starting point. Calendar-based tools connect to Google or Outlook calendars, capture activities automatically, and use custom tags plus rule-based automations to categorize work with less manual entry. That matters because the team sees time as it happens, not after someone tries to reconstruct it from memory. Why the calendar view changes the workflow A calendar gives managers early signals. If a client team is already close to the 40-hour mark, an operations lead can catch it before overtime lands in payroll. That creates a different workflow from chasing timesheets after the fact, because the action happens while the week is still open. The best overtime control is the one that starts before the sheet gets submitted. If you need a related comparison point, the IR35 timesheet essentials article shows how time capture becomes a compliance record, not just an admin task. The same logic applies here, because the quality of the record drives the quality of the payroll result. What good automation does TimeTackle also surfaces utilization data through dashboards and filters, which helps leaders see work by project, client, team, or opportunity. That matters because overtime mistakes often hide inside reporting gaps, not inside payroll math itself. A cleaner capture process gives finance and operations the same view of the week before they make a pay decision. If your team still depends on manual reporting, the Tackle time tracker overview lays out the workflow details. The point is not that software replaces judgment. The point is that software removes repetitive capture work, so judgment arrives before payroll closes. Your action plan for accurate overtime pay and compliance Start by auditing exemption status against the latest salary threshold and your state rules, then fix any role that no longer fits the current test. Next, verify that your regular rate includes bonuses, commissions, and other variable pay where required, because the overtime rate depends on that number. Define your official FLSA workweek in writing, share it with managers, and stop letting calendar weeks confuse approval habits. Then replace manual timesheets with calendar-based capture so hours show up as work happens, not after someone guesses them back into a spreadsheet. If you want a practical reference for payroll process work, the payroll management category can help teams compare common workflows and controls. Success looks like this: managers see overtime risk before payroll closes, finance trusts the rate calculation, and employees stop redoing timesheets. If you're ready to cut overtime mistakes and reduce timesheet fatigue, visit TimeTackle to see how calendar-based tracking can help your team capture hours more accurately and keep payroll cleaner. title: Vertiv announces global launch of overhead prefabricated infrastructure portfolio to accelerate data center deployment
summary: Vertiv (NYSE: VRT), a global provider of critical digital infrastructure and continuity solutions, today announced the global launch of Vertiv™ SmartRun, a modular prefabricated overhead infrastructure system designed to integrate high-density power distribution busbar, liquid cooling piping network, hot-aisle containment and network infrastructure into a single, scalable solution, supporting an accelerated data center fit-out. This all-in-one solution reduces complexity and accelerates deployment times of cloud and AI training applications for greenfield and retrofit colocation and hyperscale data centers.
body_text: Columbus, Ohio [March 18, 2025] – Vertiv (NYSE: VRT), a global provider of critical digital infrastructure and continuity solutions, today announced the global launch of Vertiv™ SmartRun , a modular prefabricated overhead infrastructure system designed to integrate high-density power distribution busbar, liquid cooling piping network, hot-aisle containment, and network infrastructure into a single, scalable solution, supporting an accelerated data center fit-out. This all-in-one solution reduces complexity and accelerates deployment times of cloud and AI training applications for greenfield and retrofit colocation and hyperscale data centers. Deploying Vertiv SmartRun delivers significant advantages in scalability and efficiency, providing end-to-end speed and adaptable configurations to meet various design requirements. With prefabricated assembly, plug-and-play design, and a simplified one-lift installation process, Vertiv SmartRun can deploy up to 85% faster on-site than traditional stick-build methods, enabling datacenter installations greater than 1MW per day with just a single crew. The pre-designed system reduces labor needs for engineering review and installation of busway, piping, network cabling, and hot-aisle containment systems, offering a streamlined approach to integrating overhead infrastructure The system also addresses the whitespace challenges of incorporating new heat removal technologies into AI datacenters, by integrating a secondary fluid network into the Vertiv SmartRun design. Prefabricated stainless steel piping systems mitigate complexity of design, fabrication, and startup, providing a single source for end-to-end data center liquid cooling support. “As digital infrastructure demands evolve, organizations require solutions that accelerate growth without adding complexity,” said Viktor Petik, senior vice president, infrastructure solutions at Vertiv. “Vertiv™ SmartRun is a strategic investment in high-density, prefabricated infrastructure that brings operational agility and enables seamless expansion to support the future of high-density computing.” Vertiv™ SmartRun is backed by Vertiv™ Liquid Cooling Services and Vertiv™ Global Services, a global network of trained experts available to provide comprehensive support for the installation, maintenance, and optimization of liquid cooled infrastructure, supporting efficient thermal management and long-term reliability in high-density environments. For more information on Vertiv SmartRun and Vertiv’s portfolio of infrastructure, power, cooling and services solutions, visit Vertiv.com . About Vertiv Vertiv (NYSE: VRT) brings together hardware, software, analytics and ongoing services to enable its customers’ vital applications to run continuously, perform optimally and grow with their business needs. Vertiv solves the most important challenges facing today’s data centers, communication networks and commercial and industrial facilities with a portfolio of power, cooling, and IT infrastructure solutions and services that extends from the cloud to the edge of the network. Headquartered in Westerville, Ohio, USA, Vertiv does business in more than 130 countries. For more information, and for the latest news and content from Vertiv, visit Vertiv.com . title: Announcing Depot Metal
summary: Depot Metal is our next-generation compute and storage platform. Depot CI and Sandboxes are now running on it, with benchmarks showing workloads 30% faster and more optimizations on the way. You don't have to do anything to get it.
body_text: Your Depot CI and Sandbox workloads just got faster thanks to Depot Metal , the next generation of our compute platform. Our benchmarks already show workloads running 30% faster, with more optimizations incoming. If you use Depot CI or Depot Sandboxes, they're already running on Depot Metal at no additional cost. What is Depot Metal? Depot Metal is the 4th iteration of our compute and storage platform, combining the learnings from all previous storage and compute at Depot into one unified platform: Bare-metal EC2 instances : from AWS, powered by 5th-generation AMD EPYC processors, running microVMs Dedicated EC2 storage instances : providing microVM root disks, backed by high-performance NVMe local SSDs AWS S3 : as the ultimate storage location for microVM disk blocks This architecture gives us direct control over each tier: direct control over compute with EC2 bare metal, ultra-fast NVMe to cache the VM disk blocks, and S3 to durably save base images and snapshots. Technical background The Depot Metal compute and storage tiers Depot Metal combines the best of Depot's previous architectures into one unified compute and storage platform. This delivers something unique within AWS: combining the fastest compute instance type with the fastest storage instance type, and replacing EBS, to create the highest performance compute platform for all Depot workloads. Compute From benchmarking, EC2 instances with AMD EPYC CPUs deliver the highest performance for build and test workloads running on Depot. This is due in part to the raw performance that the CPUs deliver, as well as the fact that each vCPU is backed by one physical CPU core; a 1 to 1 layout of CPU threads to CPU cores. This ensures that even single-threaded workloads compute quickly. EC2 bare metal also gives us direct control over the physical hardware and microVM hypervisor; Depot Metal has been tuned to take full advantage of the compute hosts. Moving to a microVM architecture allows us to run workload accelerators (for example, memory caching) and job observability outside the job VMs, directly on the host, freeing resources inside the VMs for user jobs. The new separation created by bare metal + hypervisor also allows for enhanced security, as orchestration components no longer need to run inside the VMs next to user jobs, but can now observe jobs from outside, on the metal host itself. This new architecture also dramatically decreases the time to start new workload VMs: previously each CI job would need to wait for a new EC2 host to start. We optimized this time to under 10s, but using microVMs, this can now be sub-second. Storage Up until now, we have used a few different storage technologies depending on the workflow or type of data being stored: S3 : used to store cache blobs produced by CI jobs and build tools like Bazel, Gradle, Go Distributed block device (Ceph) : used to store Docker image build cache on full block devices, backed by NVMe SSDs EBS : single-use ephemeral root disks, used for just one job and then destroyed RAM disk cache : used inside CI runners to accelerate both reads and writes from EBS using host memory Depot Metal combines the learnings of all four of these technologies into one accelerated storage platform: S3 is the ultimate durability layer for VM base images and snapshots, these are stored as real ext4 filesystems / block-level snapshots, for maximum performance and compatibility with all workloads running inside Depot Metal. Dedicated EC2 instances act as storage servers for multiple bare metal compute hosts, these servers read and write disk content from S3 and store it on high-performance local NVMe SSDs. These servers replace Ceph and EBS, delivering the microVM disks to the compute servers via NVMe-oF/TCP. Both the compute servers and the storage servers cache block reads and writes in host memory, mirroring our previous learnings from using memory as a disk cache. Using Depot Metal All Depot CI workloads and Depot Sandboxes are now running on Depot Metal ! You do not need to do anything to take advantage of the new performance. What's next? We're excited by the performance Depot Metal delivers today, and we're already working on additional optimizations. We'll migrate Depot GitHub Actions runners and container builds to Depot Metal over the next few months. And we'll share details and more technical deep dives as we go. FAQ Why did Depot launch Metal? We had been running different compute and storage technologies for different workloads: S3 for cache blobs, Ceph for Docker build cache, EBS for ephemeral root disks, and RAM disk caching on top. Depot Metal folds the learnings from all of them into one unified platform. Building on bare-metal EC2 gives Depot direct control over every tier, from the CPU and hypervisor down to the NVMe storage, which means better performance, and moving orchestration out of the job VMs also improves security. Do I need to do anything to run my workloads on Depot Metal? No. Depot CI workloads and Depot Sandboxes are already running on Depot Metal, at no additional cost. There's no config change, no opt-in, and no migration on your end. You just get the faster performance. Where does the speedup come from? A few things stack up. The AMD EPYC CPUs back each vCPU with a physical core in a 1:1 layout, so even single-threaded work runs fast. Running on bare metal with a microVM hypervisor lets Depot move accelerators like memory caching and job observability out of the job VM and onto the host, freeing resources for your work. And the storage tier replaces EBS and Ceph with NVMe-backed servers over NVMe-oF/TCP, with block reads and writes cached in host memory. Separately, microVMs start in sub-second time instead of waiting for a new EC2 host to boot, which cuts startup latency. Are Depot container builds and GitHub Actions runners running on Depot Metal too? Not yet. Today Depot Metal powers Depot CI and Depot Sandboxes. GitHub Actions runners and container builds will move to Metal over the next few months, and we'll share more technical detail as we go. Related posts Now available: Depot CI Now available: Depot Sandbox SDK Optimizing microVM boot times Jacob Gillespie CTO & Co-founder of Depot

title: Keel Infrastructure Advances Sherbrooke, Québec Data Center Project
summary: NEW YORK, July 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Keel Infrastructure Corp. (Nasdaq: KEEL; TSX: KEEL) (the “Company” or “Keel”), a North American digital infrastructure and energy company, today announced an update on its data center project in Sherbrooke, Québec.
body_text: NEW YORK, July 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Keel Infrastructure Corp. (Nasdaq: KEEL; TSX: KEEL) (the “Company” or “Keel”), a North American digital infrastructure and energy company, today announced an update on its data center project in Sherbrooke, Québec. The Company has received approval from the City of Sherbrooke to enter into an agreement with Hydro-Sherbrooke for the transfer and operation of 96 MW of existing capacity, as well as a purchase agreement for a parcel of land on which to develop the data center. The transfer of the energy capacity to the new site is now subject to review and approval by Quebec’s Ministry of Economy, Innovation and Energy (MEIE) . Power Agreement The agreement reached with Hydro-Sherbrooke will allow Keel to consolidate the power from three of its current Bitcoin mining sites into one 96 MW campus. The Company did not request any additional power, which maximizes the use of current electrical infrastructure and allows the project to move forward in line with Québec's current energy priorities. Keel also received approval to recategorize the use of its 96 MW from BTC mining to HPC/AI. Land Purchase Agreement Keel has also entered into a purchase agreement to acquire a parcel of land approximately 100 miles east of Montréal. The purchase agreement is subject to customary conditions, including site inspections, feasibility analysis, and municipal approvals, and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. “These developments represent an important step forward in the development of our Sherbrooke project, which will be one of the largest data center projects in Québec. The City’s approval of these agreements reflects the strength of the project and our commitment to the Sherbrooke community,” said Philippe Fortier, Executive Vice President, Corporate Development at Keel. “We have operated with great success in Québec since our Company’s inception, and this project reinforces our long-term commitment to contributing to both the local and broader Québec economies while delivering state-of-the-art digital infrastructure.” Keel aims to build this project on a lasting relationship with its host community. The Company looks forward to collaborating with local and regional stakeholders and will share updates on the project's progress in a spirit of open and constructive dialogue. The Company would also like to thank all partners and collaborators who contributed to reaching this milestone, including the municipal teams, Hydro-Sherbrooke, and the various stakeholders involved. About Keel Infrastructure Keel Infrastructure is a North American digital infrastructure and energy company that develops and owns data centers and energy infrastructure for high-performance computing workloads, including AI. With a pipeline of 2.2 gigawatts and established grid interconnections already in place, Keel delivers scalable infrastructure solutions in high-demand power markets across Pennsylvania and Washington in the United States, and Québec in Canada. Keel is headquartered in New York City and trades under the ticker symbol “KEEL” on Nasdaq and the TSX. Learn more at www.keelinfra.com. title: Salario mínimo en México 2026: cuánto es y cómo se calcula
summary: Salario mínimo en México 2026: $315.04 diarios en zona general y $440.87 en la frontera norte. Cifras CONASAMI, impacto y cómo cobrar en dólares.
body_text: El salario mínimo en México 2026 subió a 315.04 pesos diarios en la zona general, un aumento del 13 por ciento, pero para millones de trabajadores el problema no es solo cuánto suben las cifras: es cuánto queda después de la inflación, cuándo llega el pago y en qué moneda. La brecha entre lo que dice la ley y lo que rinde en la vida real sigue siendo el centro del debate. En esta guía verás las cifras oficiales de la Comisión Nacional de los Salarios Mínimos (CONASAMI) para 2026, cómo se calcula el aumento, su impacto en la economía y qué opciones tienen los trabajadores remotos que cobran desde el extranjero. Ontop es una plataforma global de nómina y pagos que permite a las empresas contratar y pagar equipos en más de 150 países, y a los trabajadores recibir su dinero en dólares sin fricción. Puntos clave El salario mínimo general en México para 2026 es de 315.04 pesos diarios (alrededor de 9,582 pesos al mes), un aumento del 13 por ciento frente a 2025, según CONASAMI. En la Zona Libre de la Frontera Norte el salario mínimo diario sube a 440.87 pesos (cerca de 13,410 pesos al mes), con un incremento del 5 por ciento. El aumento se calcula con el Monto Independiente de Recuperación (MIR) de 17.01 pesos más un incremento porcentual del 6.5 por ciento en la zona general. El nuevo salario mínimo entró en vigor el 1 de enero de 2026 y se publicó en el Diario Oficial de la Federación. Para los trabajadores remotos mexicanos, cobrar de clientes en el extranjero puede superar por mucho el salario mínimo local, pero el método y la moneda de pago definen cuánto rinde de verdad. Las empresas que contratan en México deben pagar al menos el mínimo vigente y cumplir con las obligaciones laborales locales para evitar riesgos. ¿Cuál es el salario mínimo en México en 2026? El salario mínimo general en México para 2026 es de 315.04 pesos diarios, equivalente a unos 9,582 pesos mensuales, según CONASAMI. En la Zona Libre de la Frontera Norte asciende a 440.87 pesos diarios, cerca de 13,410 pesos al mes. Ambas cifras entraron en vigor el 1 de enero de 2026 y aplican a todo trabajador de la formalidad. El país mantiene dos áreas geográficas para el salario mínimo. La zona general cubre la mayor parte del territorio, mientras que la Zona Libre de la Frontera Norte agrupa a los municipios cercanos a la frontera con Estados Unidos, donde el costo de vida y la cercanía con una economía más fuerte justifican un piso salarial más alto. Zona 2025 (diario) 2026 (diario) 2026 (mensual aprox.) Aumento Zona General $278.80 $315.04 $9,582 +13% Zona Libre Frontera Norte $419.88 $440.87 $13,410 +5% ¿Quién define el salario mínimo y cómo se calcula? El salario mínimo en México lo define la Comisión Nacional de los Salarios Mínimos (CONASAMI), un organismo tripartito con representación de gobierno, empleadores y trabajadores. Cada año revisa y ajusta el piso salarial considerando la inflación, el costo de la canasta básica y la situación económica, y publica el resultado en el Diario Oficial de la Federación. Para 2026, el ajuste combinó dos componentes. Primero, el Monto Independiente de Recuperación (MIR), una cantidad fija de 17.01 pesos que se suma al salario mínimo vigente antes de aplicar cualquier porcentaje. Después, sobre esa base se aplicó un incremento del 6.5 por ciento en la zona general, mientras que la Zona Libre de la Frontera Norte recibió un incremento global del 5 por ciento. El resultado es el aumento del 13 por ciento en la zona general. Este mecanismo busca recuperar el poder adquisitivo perdido durante años en los que el salario mínimo se rezagó frente al costo de vida. Aun con los aumentos recientes, muchos especialistas señalan que el mínimo sigue siendo ajustado para cubrir las necesidades de una familia. ¿Cuál es el impacto del salario mínimo en México? El impacto del salario mínimo se ve en dos niveles. A escala individual, millones de trabajadores de menores ingresos dependen de ese piso para sostener a sus familias, por lo que cada punto de aumento influye directamente en su capacidad de compra. A escala macroeconómica, un mínimo más alto puede impulsar el consumo interno y reducir la desigualdad, aunque genera debate sobre sus efectos en el empleo. Quienes defienden aumentos sostenidos argumentan que fortalecen el mercado interno y ayudan a cerrar la brecha de ingresos. Quienes advierten sobre riesgos señalan la presión sobre sectores con márgenes ajustados. En la práctica, México ha optado por una recuperación gradual y constante del salario mínimo durante los últimos años, con la meta de acercarlo al costo real de la canasta básica. Para el trabajador, el número del salario mínimo importa, pero también importa lo que ocurre después: la puntualidad del pago, las comisiones que se le descuentan y la moneda en la que recibe su dinero. Ahí es donde muchos mexicanos que trabajan a distancia buscan alternativas. ¿Cómo afecta el salario mínimo a los trabajadores remotos y freelancers? Para los trabajadores remotos mexicanos, el salario mínimo local suele ser solo un punto de referencia. Muchos cobran de empresas en Estados Unidos u otros países con salarios más altos, por lo que sus ingresos pueden superar ampliamente el mínimo nacional. El verdadero reto no es cuánto ganan en el papel, sino cómo reciben ese dinero sin perder valor en el camino. Cuando un freelancer cobra en dólares y su plataforma de pago aplica una conversión forzada a pesos con un tipo de cambio desfavorable, una parte del ingreso se evapora en el spread. Lo mismo ocurre con pagos que tardan días en llegar o con comisiones ocultas. Por eso conviene recibir y mantener el dinero en dólares y decidir cuándo convertirlo. Con una cuenta global en dólares el trabajador controla su saldo, evita conversiones automáticas y accede a su dinero cuando lo necesita. Si quieres una guía práctica sobre este tema, revisa cómo cobrar en dólares desde Latinoamérica y compara opciones según tus clientes y tu país. ¿Cómo pueden las empresas pagar cumpliendo la ley en México? Las empresas que contratan en México deben pagar al menos el salario mínimo vigente, cumplir con las contribuciones de seguridad social y respetar las obligaciones laborales locales. Para una compañía extranjera sin entidad en el país, hacerlo por cuenta propia implica trámites, riesgo de incumplimiento y demoras que frenan la contratación de talento mexicano. Ontop es una plataforma global de nómina y pagos que permite contratar y pagar talento en México cumpliendo con la normativa local, sin necesidad de abrir una entidad. La plataforma gestiona la nómina, los pagos y el cumplimiento, de modo que la empresa se enfoca en el trabajo y el profesional recibe su pago a tiempo y en la moneda que prefiera. Preguntas frecuentes ¿Cuánto es el salario mínimo diario en México en 2026? En 2026 el salario mínimo general es de 315.04 pesos diarios en la zona general y de 440.87 pesos diarios en la Zona Libre de la Frontera Norte, según CONASAMI, vigente desde el 1 de enero de 2026. ¿Cuánto es el salario mínimo mensual en México en 2026? El salario mínimo general equivale a unos 9,582 pesos mensuales en la zona general y a cerca de 13,410 pesos mensuales en la Zona Libre de la Frontera Norte, considerando un mes de 30.4 días. ¿Cuánto aumentó el salario mínimo en 2026? El salario mínimo general aumentó 13 por ciento respecto a 2025, mientras que el de la Zona Libre de la Frontera Norte subió 5 por ciento. El ajuste incluyó un Monto Independiente de Recuperación de 17.01 pesos más un incremento porcentual. ¿Los trabajadores remotos en México ganan el salario mínimo? No necesariamente. Muchos trabajadores remotos cobran de empresas en el extranjero por montos superiores al mínimo local. Lo relevante para ellos es el método, la moneda y la puntualidad del pago, más que el piso salarial nacional. Reflexiones finales El salario mínimo en México 2026 confirma una tendencia de recuperación gradual, con 315.04 pesos diarios en la zona general y 440.87 en la frontera norte. Aun así, para el trabajador lo decisivo no es solo el monto, sino cuánto rinde después de impuestos, comisiones y conversiones de moneda. title: WA - Western Alliance Bank Launches VenueX™
summary: Western Alliance Bank (NYSE: WAL), a leading national commercial bank with over $90 billion in assets, today formally announced the launch of WA VenueX™, an institutional financial platform that provides real-time U.S. dollar liquidity and supports digita
body_text: PHOENIX — Western Alliance Bank (NYSE: WAL), a leading national commercial bank with over $90 billion in assets, today formally announced the launch of WA VenueX™, an institutional financial platform that provides real-time U.S. dollar liquidity and supports digital asset activity within a regulated banking environment. WA VenueX Network™ is Western Alliance Bank’s 24/7 U.S. dollar (USD) instant settlement network for approved institutional digital asset businesses. Since its initial rollout earlier this year, WA VenueX has processed billions of dollars in transaction volume for stablecoin minting and redemption, institutional digital asset settlement and real-time liquidity rebalancing. The launch positions Western Alliance Bank among a select group of regulated U.S. financial institutions providing always-on infrastructure for institutional digital asset markets. Additional WA VenueX capabilities, including digital asset custody, financing, tokenization and programmable financial services, are in development and will be introduced in phases over the coming months. Dale Gibbons , Western Alliance Vice Chairman and Chief Banking Officer, Deposit Initiatives & Innovation, said, “Western Alliance Bank is always looking for innovative ways to better serve our clients while advancing the S-curve funding growth strategy we outlined at our Investor Day in May. WA VenueX reflects that approach by delivering scalable, compliant financial infrastructure designed for digital asset businesses that operate around the clock. In addition to providing real-time U.S. dollar liquidity, WA VenueX supports our ongoing deposit remixing efforts, contributing to a more diversified and durable source of funding while further strengthening our position as a leading banking partner to the digital asset industry.” “WA VenueX brings together real-time USD settlement and a roadmap toward integrated digital asset capabilities within a single platform,” said David Fragale , Senior Managing Director, Digital Assets Group, Western Alliance Bank. “With WA VenueX Network live and already processing billions in transaction volume, clients currently access always-on USD liquidity and can prepare for broader digital asset workflows as the platform evolves. Ultimately, WA VenueX will be a one-stop hub inside the bank for the digital assets ecosystem.” Global financial markets increasingly operate around the clock, while many traditional banking processes continue to rely on cutoffs, batch processing and business-day settlement windows. WA VenueX Network addresses this gap by enabling continuous, real-time U.S. dollar settlement through Western Alliance Bank, allowing network participants to move capital without interruption and align liquidity with global market activity. Why Clients Choose WA VenueX "Coinbase is proud to work with Western Alliance and leverage WA VenueX as part of our 24/7 operating model. Reliable, around-the-clock access to U.S. dollar liquidity is critical for institutional participants, and WA VenueX delivers that capability within a trusted banking framework. We believe platforms like WA VenueX will play a foundational role in the continued growth of the digital asset ecosystem, and we look forward to contributing to a more connected, efficient and always-on financial system.” - Liz Martin, Coinbase VP of Markets Expanding to a Unified Institutional Financial Platform WA VenueX is designed to evolve beyond real-time settlement into a broader platform integrating digital asset custody, financing and tokenization within a single banking environment. As these capabilities are introduced in the future, WA VenueX is intended to help firms manage liquidity and deploy capital across fiat and digital asset markets within a unified, always-on system. Planned capabilities include support for stablecoin-related workflows, digital asset–backed financing and tokenized asset structures. A Platform Built for Institutional Scale Western Alliance introduces WA VenueX with nearly five years of digital asset banking experience and approximately 150 institutional clients, including stablecoin issuers, exchanges and trading firms. As adoption grows, WA VenueX Network is expected to benefit from increasing liquidity and connectivity across participants. WA VenueX Network is currently available to select Digital Assets clients, with broader platform capabilities expected to roll out over time. Integration is supported via API through Western Alliance Bank’s Digital Asset Banking team. Learn more about Western Alliance Bank About Us Western Alliance Bank Western Alliance Bancorporation (NYSE: WAL) is one of the country’s top-performing banking companies and has ranked as a top U.S. bank by American Banker and Bank Director since 2016. Its primary subsidiary, Western Alliance Bank, is a leading national bank for business that puts customers first, delivering tailored business banking solutions and consumer products backed by outstanding, personalized service and specific expertise in more than 30 industries and sectors.
